item.title: Brewers Star Becomes Youngest Player To Do This In 80 Years
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers outfielder Jackson Chourio The Milwaukee Brewers made a lot of World Series history in Game 3 on Monday night, including Jackson Chourio. The 22-year-old outfielder continued his torrid World Series, going 4-for-5 and pacing the Brewers' 10-1 rout of the Tampa Bay Rays at Tropicana Field. Milwaukee's leadoff man doubled, scored two runs, drove in one and stole a base, doing a little bit of everything. In the process, Chourio became the youngest player with four hits in a World Series game since Joe Garagiola, who went 4-for-5 in Game 4 of the 1946 World Series as a 20-year-old rookie catcher for the St. Louis Cardinals. He's the fifth-youngest player with at least four hits in a World Series game in MLB history. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? item.title: Yuri Yoshida is the latest LPGA winner in a golden era for Japanese women’s golf
item.description: This is turning into a golden era for the Land of the Rising Sun on the LPGA Tour. Yuri Yoshida hit a pitching wedge from 48 yards to a back pin on an elevated green to 4 feet, a sublime shot that effectively secured her first LPGA Tour title at the BMW Ladies Championship in South Korea. Yoshida became the fifth first-time winner on the LPGA this season, and the third from Japan. Her victory came a month after Yuna Nishimura won in Arkansas. And in August, Shiho Kuwaki captured her first major at the Women’s British Open. But it goes back further than this year. Japanese players have won five of the last 15 majors over the last three years, two more than players from South Korea and one player (Nelly Korda) from the United States — Yuka Saso (U.S. Women’s Open), Mao Saigo (Chevron), Miyu Yamashita and Kuwaki (Women’s British Open), and Ayaka Furue (Evian). The last two years on the LPGA have seen nine different players from Japan winning official events. South Korea, which has dominated the LPGA the last three decades, still has the depth with 14 players among the top 50 in the women’s world ranking. Japan is next with 10 players. Most of them get plenty of preparation on the Japan LPGA. Saigo and Yamashita each won five times in 2022. Yamashita won five more times on the JLPGA in 2023 and now is No. 4 in the world, the highest ranking among Japanese players. Kuwaki won three times on the JLPGA in 2024 and two years later became a major champion. Along with her Women’s British Open title at Royal Lytham & St. Annes, Kuwaki won Sunday for her fourth JLPGA title of the year, the most of any player. Next is Shuri Sakuma with three wins. Sakuma won four times last year, and might be a name worth remembering. 02:05 Yoshida rallies to claim first LPGA Tour victory at BMW Yuri Yoshida came from behind at the BMW Championship to claim the first LPGA Tour victory of her career.

item.title: How Kane's Ballon d'Or win could boost the Bundesliga
item.description: Harry Kane is the first English winner of the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001 [AFP via Getty Images] England has had to wait a long time for another winner of the Ballon d'Or, with Harry Kane on Monday night becoming the first player from the country to win it for 25 years. But his success has also been celebrated in Germany with the Bayern Munich striker ending their even longer run without a player from the Bundesliga lifting the coveted trophy. The last to do so was Matthias Sammer back in 1996 after he had captained Borussia Dortmund to two successive Bundesliga titles. "Just as Bayern and the Bundesliga benefit from Kane, the reverse is also true," Lothar Matthaus, the most capped German player of all time and 1991 Ballon d'Or winner, said. "I don't think Kane would've won the Ballon d'Or at any other club he could've joined. He's developed further at Bayern and matured even more. "He's become a better player there, as he himself said in his speech. At Bayern, he won his very first title, with more to follow - and now he's fulfilled a lifelong dream." Name every men's Ballon d'Or winner What it means for Bayern and the Bundesliga For Kane, the trophy win will have felt special for many reasons on a personal level, having gone through ups and downs in his career to make it to the very top. But both the Bundesliga and Bayern know how significant it will also be for the league and the club respectively. After Kane was announced as the Ballon d'Or winner, large images from the Bundesliga were projected on to landmarks across London such as The Strand and Tate Modern, some featuring the words "England Hero. Bundesliga Legend". For the league, Kane's win will show players that they can come to the Bundesliga and become recognised as the best player in the world, while for Bayern it will show they are capable of attracting the very best talent. Bundesliga chief executive Marc Lenz said: "Winning the Ballon d'Or is a tremendous recognition of Harry Kane's extraordinary performances - and also a great success for Bayern and the Bundesliga. "Harry is not only one of the outstanding players of his generation; he combines sporting excellence with tremendous professionalism, commitment and respect for the game. He gives everything for his team and inspires fans around the world. "He is a fantastic role model for young players and an outstanding ambassador for the Bundesliga. "This achievement also underlines that the Bundesliga is a stage where the very best players in the world perform at the highest level." Bayern chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen added: "For a player from a German club to win the Ballon d'Or for the first time in 30 years is a strong signal for the Bundesliga," he said. item.title: Iraola aware Liverpool still have work to do despite winning run
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Liverpool manager Andoni Iraola gestures on the touchline during the English Premier League soccer match between Liverpool and Fulham at Anfield. (is associated with: «Iraola aware Liverpool still have work to do despite winning run») Peter Byrne/PA Wire/dpa Andoni Iraola is growing into the role as Liverpool head coach but accepts he needs more wins to really start feeling at home. Momentum is growing after four successive wins in all competitions, and eight in 10 since opening the season with two draws, but the Basque acknowledges there is plenty of work still to do. Iraola allowed himself a moment after Sunday’s 2-0 victory over Brighton to celebrate in front of the Kop for the first time, but he is well aware it does not take much for the confidence to be broken. “It is not to gain the confidence. I said it since the first day, you have to earn the right to belong and you only get it with good performances, with wins, and this will take time,” Iraola said, speaking ahead of Wednesday’s League Cup visit of a Chelsea team coached by his good friend Xabi Alonso. “But I am glad because I felt the other day the supporters helped us a lot and they were enjoying it the same as we were. “A start, yes. I would say a start – still we need more wins, we need more performances so we need more time.” Having come up against one of his best friends in football in Inigo Perez in last week’s Champions League tie against Villarreal he will welcome two more this week in Alonso and, on Sunday, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta. “We were close friends, we grew up together, we played in the same team, we played against each other, we played together in the national team with Spain and the Basque Country,” Iraola added of Alonso. “But now he is the opposition and we want to beat him, in the same way he will do with us. “After the game we can talk, definitely.” One of the challenges Andoni has had to adapt to since arriving from Bournemouth is playing three games a week. He is likely to make changes again for the League Cup tie but admits he cannot afford to look too deeply into the permutations of managing the squad for upcoming games. Florian Wirtz is expected to be fit after his ankle problem at the weekend but winger Victor Muñoz and Dominik Szoboszlai remain doubtful. “We have some games where we have less time to rest than the opposition but you have to adapt,” Iraola said. “It is a matter of adaptation and you cannot overthink it: analyse straight away what happened but in one hour (clicking his fingers) the next game and you have to be ready for this.”

item.title: Brewers on verge of completing playoff feat never done before in MLB history
item.description: Mark Hoffman/Milwaukee Journal Sentinel / USA TODAY NETWORK via Imagn Images Brewers on verge of completing playoff feat never done before in MLB history appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Brewers are now just one win away from winning the World Series. Milwaukee dominated the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 3 Monday, 10-1. Milwaukee now has a 3-0 series lead, and is on the verge of history. “No team has swept both the LCS and World Series since the LCS became best-of-7 in 1985….yet,” MLB reporter Sarah Langs posted to X, formerly Twitter. The Brewers swept the Los Angeles Dodgers in the NLCS, in four games. Milwaukee now has a chance to sweep Tampa. The Brewers have flexed their power throughout the entire postseason. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brewers manager Pat Murphy is in awe of what his team is doing right now. “It was unbelievable, and our players felt it, and they’ll tell you about it,” Murphy said, per MLB.com. “The players looked around like, ‘Wow!’ … That’s a statement about how much this team has captured the hearts of the people from Milwaukee and the state of Wisconsin, all the Brewer fans. It was amazing, the level of support we got tonight. It was incredible.” Milwaukee is simply unstoppable at scoring runs. The Brewers have come back from deficits many times during this year’s playoffs. Milwaukee hasn’t even needed home runs to do it. In Game 3, the Brewers posted 10 runs without any player hitting a homer. “That’s just the credit to these guys and the way they play the game,” Brewers hitting coach Dan Vogelbach said. “They just don’t play the game in the batter’s box. Offense is way more than just hitting. These guys play for each other, and nobody wants to be the hero. They’re OK with the next guy being it. They just pass the baton over and over again, and they’re getting rewarded for it.” Game 4 of the World Series is on Tuesday night. Time will tell if the Brewers do indeed make history . item.title: Florian Wirtz faces Liverpool fitness race as he battles ankle injury
item.description: Liverpool will make a late call whether to select Florian Wirtz in their Carabao Cup tie against Chelsea . The German has an ankle problem and while manager Andoni Iraola hopes he will be available to play, he is not sure. But Dominik Szoboszlai and Victor Munoz are major fitness doubts with thigh and knee problems respectively which have forced them to miss Liverpool’s last two games. “Florian, I’m quite optimistic that he will be available,” said manager Iraola. “And with Dom and Victor, I’m not so sure. I don’t want to say no, but I think it’s going to be more difficult than Florian, yes.” Wirtz is still waiting for his first goal against Premier League clubs this season after he seemed to open the scoring at home to Brighton on Sunday , only for it to go down as an own goal by Pascal Gross. Liverpool will still be without the injured quartet of Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley, Giovanni Leoni and Jeremie Frimpong. Florian Wirtz is still waiting for his first goal against a Premier League club this season (Reuters) Iraola is set to rotate which could mean players such as Lewis Koumas, Trey Nyoni, Rio Ngumoha and Kostas Tsimikas come in. He added: “There will definitely be changes. But we want to win the game, we want to be competitive.” Chelsea will be without Cole Palmer, who is suspended after his sending off against Tottenham on Saturday. But while they have a poor disciplinary record in recent years, Iraola insisted he will not send Liverpool out to wind Chelsea up or try and provoke them. He added: “It is not going to be in our team meeting, we will not say anything.”

Looking at the Rockets’ schedule , a two-week hiatus would see Adams miss seven games, possibly back in time for a clash with Rockets rivals, the Golden State Warriors on November 11th, and an NBA Cup Night game versus the Utah Jazz on November 13th. Of the games he may or may not miss, the Rockets would probably miss him most for a Denver Nuggets showdown on November 9th. item.title: Paul Pierce’s Lawyer Claims Former NBA Star Is ‘Tapped Out’ and ‘Drowning Financially’
item.description: MEGA Former pro basketball player Paul Pierce claims he is facing financial hardship. A lawyer for Pierce, 49 — who spent the majority of his NBA career playing for the Boston Celtics — claimed the athlete is “drowning financially” and is having trouble keeping up with his finances, according to court documents obtained Tuesday, October 27, by TMZ . Following Pierce’s time in the NBA, he joined ESPN as a studio analyst in 2017. However, he was allegedly fired by the company in 2021 after he posted a racy Instagram Live, according to CNN . Pierce joined Fox Sports 1 as a basketball analyst in 2024, but according to TMZ, he is no longer receiving income from the company. Per the court docs, Paul claimed he received his last Fox Sports paycheck in August after bringing in an average monthly income of $119,000. Last month, he reportedly earned $23,000 from partnership interests in other business ventures. However, he allegedly must pay approximately $28,000 in child support as well as $20,000 in spousal support per month. TMZ reported in September that Pierce — who shares son King Rafael with Princess Santiago — was ordered to pay Santiago $8,508 per month in temporary child support for their son as well as $100,000 in legal fees. Lisa OConnor/AFF-USA.com / MEGA Per People , Pierce also shares three children with his ex-wife, Julie Landrum . Paul is requesting to not pay Santiago’s request for $40,000 in legal fees as well as $10,000 for a forensic accountant, per TMZ. Santiago reportedly wanted an expert to review Paul’s finances (he was said to be earning $200 million during his NBA career). The former basketball player claimed, per TMZ, that he only has $300,000 in the bank in addition to $3 million in property. As for his bills, he allegedly spends around $48,000 per month. That includes $8,000 in childcare, $7,000 on eating out, $5,000 in groceries, $3,500 on entertainment, $3,200 on utilities and $1,000 on clothes, among other things. Per TMZ, Paul’s lawyer claimed the former Los Angeles Clippers player is having “great difficulty” paying the aforementioned fees and is “tapped out” financially. It appears that Paul has yet to publicly address the financial hardships. item.title: Early Arsenal team news vs Fleetwood Town: 4 youth players called up
item.description: Early Arsenal team news vs Fleetwood Town: 4 youth players called up Mikel Arteta has reportedly called up four youth players to his Arsenal first-team squad to face Fleetwood Town, in addition to Marli Salmon and Max Dowman. Photo via Washington on Instagram Isaan Khan of the Daily Mail reports that Arsenal youth quartet Ceadach O’Neill , Maalik Hashi , Andre Harriman-Annous , and Marcell Washington are all set to be in the first-team squad to face Fleetwood Town in the fourth round of the League Cup on Tuesday night. Khan adds that Marli Salmon and Max Dowman will also be included, and the pair are likely to start the match. The report follows rumours on social media that O’Neill is set to start as well, though this remains unconfirmed at this stage. Photo by Cameron Howard/Getty Images Arsenal fans will already be well aware of young centre-back Salmon and midfielder/winger Dowman, and supporters who followed pre-season closely would also have had a look at 18-year-old forward O’Neill. O’Neill has already made the senior squad this season, featuring on the bench against Lille . He also made the bench for two of Arsenal’s FA Cup matches last season. But the teenager is yet to make his on-field debut, and that could be set to change on Tuesday. Primarily a centre-forward, O’Neill is also capable of playing on the wings. Photo by Cameron Howard/Getty Images Fellow versatile forward Harriman-Annous made his first Arsenal start in the League Cup last season, before making his Champions League debut from the bench against Slavia Praha . Then midfielder Hashi and left-back Washington are both waiting on their first senior appearances. There’s hardly going to be a better opportunity than against Fleetwood on Tuesday night. item.title: ‘He knows he made a big mistake’: Carragher says he would welcome Alexander-Arnold back at Liverpool
item.description: ‘He knows he made a big mistake’: Carragher says he would welcome Alexander-Arnold back at Liverpool Jamie Carragher has said he would take Trent Alexander-Arnold back at Liverpool and believes the defender knows 'he made a big mistake' by leaving for Real Madrid . Alexander-Arnold left Liverpool for Real Madrid in 2025, after running down his contract at Anfield. The right-back's decision to leave and circumstances around his exit received fierce backlash from the club's supports. The 28-year-old has struggled to live up to expectations in Spanish football and has started just three La Liga games this season. Alexander-Arnold was used only as a late substitute during Real Madrid's crucial 2-1 win at Barcelona at the weekend. There has been tentative talk of a potential return to the Reds for the defender, and Carragher believes it could be a sensible move. He said Liverpool have missed Alexander-Arnold's creativity from full-back and believes the England international could solve several issues for Andoni Iraola's side. “At the moment, he’s third-choice right-back for Real Madrid. When you’re third choice at a club, they’re obviously wanting you to move on," Carragher told The Overlap Fan Debate. “I’d have him back. I think he made a big mistake leaving. But if something benefits Liverpool Football Club going forward, when you think of the problems Liverpool have at right-back… “Ronald Araújo has been fantastic, but we do have a problem in terms of the full-backs’ passing. We’ve definitely missed Trent’s creativity.”

item.title: Greenfield sports store feeling positives, negatives of Brewers run
item.description: Jordyn Lang is getting good at delivering bad news. Since the Milwaukee Brewers won the National League pennant, the manager at Green and Gold Zone has found herself constantly explaining to customers the realities a small sports merchandise store faces in these historic times. She did it more than five times in half an hour on Oct. 26, the same 30-second conversation every time. The phone would ring, Lang would answer. Five seconds later, after the customer asked the question she knew was coming, Lang would regurgitate what's become a sort of company line as of late: They had very little Brewers World Series gear in stock, and she didn't know when more would arrive. "We've been pretty much picked through," Lang explained to one caller. "Like everyone else." Green and Gold Zone, at 4862 S. 74th St. in Greenfield, is first and foremost a Green Bay Packers store. But right now, the Packers are not the most relevant Wisconsin sports team. Not while the Brewers are one win from their first-ever World Series title after decades of toiling in baseball purgatory. All this never-before-seen success is prompting fans to open their wallets and buy never-before-seen amounts of swag . The sports apparel giants of the world − like Fanatics − can prepare for and match the unprecedented demand. Local, family-owned companies − like Green and Gold Zone − cannot. Owner Amy Hundt said it usually takes around 3 to 5 days to receive special merch; the Brewers won Game 4 of the NLCS on a Thursday, and boxes of World Series gear arrived the following Monday. Three days later, pretty much all of it was sold, with shirts and hats being the first items to go. "The Brewers are taking the spotlight right now," Hundt said. The last week-and-a-half, Green and Gold Zone has operated more like a blue and gold zone, selling more Brewers merch than anything else. Perhaps a temporary name change is in order. "We've thought about that," Hundt said. Customers sure are treating it like a Brewers store, showing up in Crew gear and heading straight to where they can buy more. They don't need to travel far. Directly inside the entrance are two long lines of racks with only Brewers NLCS shirts. Some are from 2026, but most now say 2025 or don't have a year at all. To the left of the doors is a table with 2026 National League Champions items, including flags of multiple sizes and colors, along with decals and pins. That's about it for World Series merchandise until the vendor delivers a new shipment, which Hundt hopes will happen sooner rather than later. There are multiple shelves on the right side of the store dedicated to the Brewers, but they all hold generic gear. Jean Uttke learned that the hard way. The 64-year-old Brewers fan walked in and went straight to the hat section, hoping to buy one with "World Series" written across the side for her brother, who lives in Phoenix. item.title: Mark Cuban reveals what actually made him sell the Dallas Mavericks
item.description: Photo by Ron Jenkins/Getty Images After spending a lifetime chasing the next multi-million-dollar deal, Mark Cuban finally found something money couldn’t buy him. Mark Cuban jumped into the deep end back in January 2000, shelling out $285 million to buy the Mavericks when they were basically a punchline. Over the next 24 years, he poured everything into the team, turned the culture around, and finally got his hands on a ring in 2011. But after nearly a quarter-century running the show courtside, he decided to cash in. In late 2023, he sold his controlling stake to the Adelson and Dumont families in a massive deal valuing the franchise at around $3.5 billion, walking away with a staggering profit. Mark Cuban values family time over investments Mark Cuban was refreshingly blunt about why he pulled the ripcord on the Dallas Mavericks . Getting older forced him to look in the mirror, and suddenly, skipping family birthdays for boardroom meetings felt like a bad joke. Seeing how fast his three kids were growing up, he just couldn’t justify the grind anymore. Talking on the Diary of a CEO YouTube channel, he said: “When you start feeling your own mortality and you start recognising what’s important, my kids, my family, that next business trip didn’t seem nearly as important as it used to. Missing a birthday and telling myself, well, I’ll be there for the next one, became a mistake. I was just like what’s the point of doing this? “They were 13, 16 and 19 when I sold the Mavs and a little bit older when I got out of Shark Tank. It wasn’t going to be all that long till they were on their own and I just wanted to be there as much as I could.” The keys now belong to Miriam Adelson and her son-in-law Patrick Dumont, who calls the shots as governor. And they couldn’t have scripted a better start, either, as the Mavs went on a tear straight to the NBA Finals in 2024, proving the front office didn’t miss a beat post-Cuban.
